WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE.
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Gorontalo Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Gorontalo.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
4. Regional Governance is the administration of government affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or ...
11. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Region to provide services in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
16. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and ... in the household.
19. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.

Article 11
Other violence as referred to in Article 5 letter f is committed due to:
a. threats of violence, which include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrain a person's fundamental freedom; and coercion, which includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something that is contrary to their own will.

Article 14
(1) The Regional Government is obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through:
a. policy determination,
b. formulation of program and activity planning,
c. providing support for facilities and infrastructure,
d. providing support for facilities and infrastructure, and
e. allocating budget,
f. establishment of Children's Forum, and
g. establishment of Task Force.

a. facilitating the establishment of P2TP2A,
b. facilitating facilities and infrastructure of P2TP2A according to the capacity of the Region, and
c. facilitating the Task Force as a network forum for handling Victims.

Article 4
The scope of this Regional Regulation includes prevention efforts, services and empowerment of victims of violence in the Region.

b. provide services to Victims, and

CHAPTER VII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 39
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for Victims.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. establishing family partners at the kelurahan/village level by the community,
b. establishing women and children protection units within community organizations,
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights,
d. providing first aid to victims,
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

Article 38
The duties and functions of FPKK as referred to in Article 37 paragraph (1) are:
a. coordinating and synchronizing prevention, services, and empowerment for victims of violence against women and children,
b. maintaining and developing FPKK in prevention, services, and empowerment of victims of violence through networking and a referral system,
c. conducting education on non-discrimination values toward women and children,
d. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence,
e. collecting, compiling, and presenting reports on data of victims of violence, and
f. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

Article 13
Child victims of violence, in addition to receiving the rights as referred to in Article 12, also receive special rights, consisting of:
a. respect for survival, growth and development, basic services, equal protection, being free from various stigma, and/or obtaining liberty.

Article 36
(1) Regional Government, P2TP2A, and the community are obligated to fulfill the rights of child victims of violence.
(2) The form of fulfillment of the rights of child victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes the fulfillment of basic rights of children in accordance with their needs.

NUMBER 4 YEAR 2018
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

II. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent disposition, without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

Article 6
Physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a results in injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death.

Article 9
Neglect as referred to in Article 5 letter d is caused by:
a. acts that result in the failure to properly fulfill a child’s needs, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for the child’s care,
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for the child’s care,
c. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of their household, whereas under the law applicable to them or due to consent or an agreement they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person, and/or,
d. acts that result in economic dependency by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under that person’s control.

Article 10
Exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter e is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial, and/or all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecent acts.

CHAPTER III
RIGHTS OF VICTIMS
Article 12
Every Victim has the right:
a. to have their dignity and worth as a human being respected;
b. health and psychological recovery from the suffering experienced by the victim; to determine their own decisions, to obtain information, confidentiality of their identity, compensation, social rehabilitation, complaint handling, to obtain facilitation in the judicial process, and/or assistance.

II. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent disposition, without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

II. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent disposition, without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

II. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent disposition, without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

c. conducting education on non-discrimination values toward women and children,
d. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence,
e. collecting, compiling, and presenting reports on data of victims of violence, and
f. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

II. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent disposition, without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

Article 16
The community and family have obligations and responsibilities which include:
a. preventing the occurrence of violence against women and children,
b. reporting if violence occurs, protecting victims; and
d. providing emergency assistance.

Article 3
Victim Protection aims to:
a. prevent violence against women and children,
b. provide services to Victims, and
c. carry out empowerment of women victims of violence.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Gorontalo Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Gorontalo.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
4. Regional Governance is the administration of government affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or ...
11. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Region to provide services in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
16. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and ... in the household.
19. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.

Article 39

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

Article 38

c. conducting education on non-discrimination values toward women and children,
d. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence,
e. collecting, compiling, and presenting reports on data of victims of violence, and
f. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

II. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent disposition, without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

Article 40

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

II. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent disposition, without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

b. safely and comfortably,

f. coordinating with other companions, and

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

II. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent disposition, without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

Article 37
(1) In an effort to protect and provide handling services for victims, the Regional Government establishes FPKK.
(2) FPKK as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of:
   a. Regional FPKK;
   b. Sub-district FPKK; and
   c. Urban Village/Village FPKK.
(3) The establishment of Regional FPKK as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a shall be stipulated by a Regent's Decree.
(4) The establishment of Sub-district FPKK as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b shall be stipulated by a Sub-district Head's Decree.
(5) The establishment of Urban Village/Village FPKK as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be stipulated by an Urban Village Head/Village Head's Decree.
(6) Further provisions regarding the organizational structure and elements of FPKK shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 15
The Regional Government is obligated and responsible to: a. supervise the implementation of services for victims, with minimum service standards, and
b. provide budget for victim protection through APBD and/or other legitimate Regional financial sources.

Article 18
(1) The Gorontalo Regency Government provides a Safe House as a form of service and protection for victims of violence through P2TP2A.
(2) The safe house referred to in paragraph (1) is equipped with facilities and infrastructure.

Article 20
(1) P2TP2A formed by the Regional Government shall have at least three counselors.
(2) Counselors as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
   a. counselors in the field of law,
   b. counselors in the field of health; and
   c. counselors in the field of psychology.
   d. counselors in other fields.
(3) The implementation of counseling carried out by counselors may be conducted in a networked manner as follows:
   a. counseling in the field of law involving the Police, the Prosecutor's Office, the District Court, the Religious Court, the Regional Government Legal Division, Legal Advocacy Institutions, and Lengan Sadang Masyarakat.
   b. counseling in the field of health involving the Health Office, the Regional General Hospital, and other health services,
   c. counseling in the field of psychology involving psychological companions and/or psychologists.

Article 4
The scope of this Regional Regulation includes prevention efforts, services and empowerment of victims of violence in the Region.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Gorontalo Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Gorontalo.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
4. Regional Governance is the administration of government affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or ...
11. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Region to provide services in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
16. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and ... in the household.
19. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.

Article 3
Victim Protection aims to:
a. prevent violence against women and children,
b. provide services to Victims, and
c. carry out empowerment of women victims of violence.

CHAPTER III
RIGHTS OF VICTIMS
Article 12
Every Victim has the right:
a. to have their dignity and worth as a human being respected;
b. health and psychological recovery from the suffering experienced by the victim; to determine their own decisions, to obtain information, confidentiality of their identity, compensation, social rehabilitation, complaint handling, to obtain facilitation in the judicial process, and/or assistance.

Article 30
(1) Legal services as referred to in Article 25 letter e are intended to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process.
(2) Legal services as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process,
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and assisting victims to comprehensively describe the violence they have experienced,
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Article 4
The scope of this Regional Regulation includes prevention efforts, services and empowerment of victims of violence in the Region.

Article 13
Child victims of violence, in addition to receiving the rights as referred to in Article 12, also receive special rights, consisting of:
a. respect for survival, growth and development, basic services, equal protection, being free from various stigma, and/or obtaining liberty.

Article 18
(1) The Gorontalo Regency Government provides a Safe House as a form of service and protection for victims of violence through P2TP2A.
(2) The safe house referred to in paragraph (1) is equipped with facilities and infrastructure.

Article 36
(1) Regional Government, P2TP2A, and the community are obligated to fulfill the rights of child victims of violence.
(2) The form of fulfillment of the rights of child victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes the fulfillment of basic rights of children in accordance with their needs.

Article 21
(1) Efforts to prevent violence against women and children shall be carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government coordinated by the regional apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by:
a. establishing a working network in efforts to prevent violence,
b. the working network referred to in point 1 (one) is:
1) task force on acts of violence against women and children,
2) Bele lomongoditi moli,
3) Children's Forum,
4) Berlian (Bersama Lindungi Anak), and
5) Suami sayang istri,
c. establishing a violence prevention system:
d. conducting socialization regarding laws and regulations related to the protection of women and children victims of violence, and
e. providing critical education on the rights of women and children for the community.
(3) The establishment of Institutions and Procedures for implementing the tasks of the working network as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 11
Other violence as referred to in Article 5 letter f is committed due to:
a. threats of violence, which include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrain a person's fundamental freedom; and coercion, which includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something that is contrary to their own will.

13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.

17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and ... in the household.

II. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent disposition, without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

II. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent disposition, without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

Article 21
(1) Efforts to prevent violence against women and children shall be carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government coordinated by the regional apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by:
a. establishing a working network in efforts to prevent violence,
b. the working network referred to in point 1 (one) is:
1) task force on acts of violence against women and children,
2) Bele lomongoditi moli,
3) Children's Forum,
4) Berlian (Bersama Lindungi Anak), and
5) Suami sayang istri,
c. establishing a violence prevention system:
d. conducting socialization regarding laws and regulations related to the protection of women and children victims of violence, and
e. providing critical education on the rights of women and children for the community.
(3) The establishment of Institutions and Procedures for implementing the tasks of the working network as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

II. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent disposition, without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

Article 3

e. allocating budget,
f. establishment of Children's Forum, and
g. establishment of Task Force.
(2) To anticipate the occurrence of acts of violence, the Regional Government organizes services for victims in the form of:
a. facilitating the establishment of P2TP2A,

Article 39
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for Victims.

a. establishing family partners at the kelurahan/village level by the community,
b. establishing women and children protection units within community organizations,
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights,
d. providing first aid to victims,
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

II. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent disposition, without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

Article 30

(2) Legal services as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process,
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and assisting victims to comprehensively describe the violence they have experienced,
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Article 16
The community and family have obligations and responsibilities which include:
a. preventing the occurrence of violence against women and children,
b. reporting if violence occurs, protecting victims; and
d. providing emergency assistance.

II. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent disposition, without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and assisting victims to comprehensively describe the violence they have experienced,
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Article 13
Child victims of violence, in addition to receiving the rights as referred to in Article 12, also receive special rights, consisting of:
a. respect for survival, growth and development, basic services, equal protection, being free from various stigma, and/or obtaining liberty.

5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.

7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.

10. Victim is women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or ...
11. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Region to provide services in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
16. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and ... in the household.
19. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.

II. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent disposition, without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

Article 36

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

Article 21
(1) Efforts to prevent violence against women and children shall be carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government coordinated by the regional apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by:
a. establishing a working network in efforts to prevent violence,
b. the working network referred to in point 1 (one) is:
1) task force on acts of violence against women and children,
2) Bele lomongoditi moli,
3) Children's Forum,
4) Berlian (Bersama Lindungi Anak), and
5) Suami sayang istri,
c. establishing a violence prevention system:
d. conducting socialization regarding laws and regulations related to the protection of women and children victims of violence, and
e. providing critical education on the rights of women and children for the community.
(3) The establishment of Institutions and Procedures for implementing the tasks of the working network as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 39
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for Victims.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. establishing family partners at the kelurahan/village level by the community,
b. establishing women and children protection units within community organizations,
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights,
d. providing first aid to victims,
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

II. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent disposition, without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE.
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Gorontalo Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Gorontalo.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
4. Regional Governance is the administration of government affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or ...
11. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Region to provide services in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
16. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and ... in the household.
19. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.

Article 14
(1) The Regional Government is obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through:
a. policy determination,
b. formulation of program and activity planning,
c. providing support for facilities and infrastructure,
d. providing support for facilities and infrastructure, and
e. allocating budget,
f. establishment of Children's Forum, and
g. establishment of Task Force.
(2) To anticipate the occurrence of acts of violence, the Regional Government organizes services for victims in the form of:
a. facilitating the establishment of P2TP2A,
b. facilitating facilities and infrastructure of P2TP2A according to the capacity of the Region, and
c. facilitating the Task Force as a network forum for handling Victims.

CHAPTER VII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 39
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for Victims.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. establishing family partners at the kelurahan/village level by the community,
b. establishing women and children protection units within community organizations,
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights,
d. providing first aid to victims,
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

Article 16
The community and family have obligations and responsibilities which include:
a. preventing the occurrence of violence against women and children,
b. reporting if violence occurs, protecting victims; and
d. providing emergency assistance.

Article 21
(1) Efforts to prevent violence against women and children shall be carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government coordinated by the regional apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by:
a. establishing a working network in efforts to prevent violence,
b. the working network referred to in point 1 (one) is:
1) task force on acts of violence against women and children,
2) Bele lomongoditi moli,
3) Children's Forum,
4) Berlian (Bersama Lindungi Anak), and
5) Suami sayang istri,
c. establishing a violence prevention system:
d. conducting socialization regarding laws and regulations related to the protection of women and children victims of violence, and
e. providing critical education on the rights of women and children for the community.
(3) The establishment of Institutions and Procedures for implementing the tasks of the working network as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 3
Victim Protection aims to:
a. prevent violence against women and children,
b. provide services to Victims, and
c. carry out empowerment of women victims of violence.

CHAPTER VIII
CLOSING PROVISIONS
Article 40
At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, all implementing regulations related to the protection of Women and Children in the Region are declared to remain valid insofar as they have not been replaced and do not conflict with the provisions in this Regional Regulation.

Paragraph 1
Empowerment of Women Victims of Violence

Article 38
The duties and functions of FPKK as referred to in Article 37 paragraph (1) are:
a. coordinating and synchronizing prevention, services, and empowerment for victims of violence against women and children,
b. maintaining and developing FPKK in prevention, services, and empowerment of victims of violence through networking and a referral system,
c. conducting education on non-discrimination values toward women and children,
d. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence,
e. collecting, compiling, and presenting reports on data of victims of violence, and
f. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF GORONTALO REGENCY
NUMBER 4 YEAR 2018
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

II. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent disposition, without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

CHAPTER VII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 39
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for Victims.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. establishing family partners at the kelurahan/village level by the community,
b. establishing women and children protection units within community organizations,
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights,
d. providing first aid to victims,
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

Article 21
(1) Efforts to prevent violence against women and children shall be carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government coordinated by the regional apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by:
a. establishing a working network in efforts to prevent violence,
b. the working network referred to in point 1 (one) is:
1) task force on acts of violence against women and children,
2) Bele lomongoditi moli,
3) Children's Forum,
4) Berlian (Bersama Lindungi Anak), and
5) Suami sayang istri,
c. establishing a violence prevention system:
d. conducting socialization regarding laws and regulations related to the protection of women and children victims of violence, and
e. providing critical education on the rights of women and children for the community.
(3) The establishment of Institutions and Procedures for implementing the tasks of the working network as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 14
(1) The Regional Government is obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children victims of violence through:
a. policy determination,
b. formulation of program and activity planning,
c. providing support for facilities and infrastructure,
d. providing support for facilities and infrastructure, and
e. allocating budget,
f. establishment of Children's Forum, and
g. establishment of Task Force.
(2) To anticipate the occurrence of acts of violence, the Regional Government organizes services for victims in the form of:
a. facilitating the establishment of P2TP2A,
b. facilitating facilities and infrastructure of P2TP2A according to the capacity of the Region, and
c. facilitating the Task Force as a network forum for handling Victims.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Gorontalo Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Gorontalo.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
4. Regional Governance is the administration of government affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or ...
11. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Region to provide services in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
16. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and ... in the household.
19. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.

Article 16
The community and family have obligations and responsibilities which include:
a. preventing the occurrence of violence against women and children,
b. reporting if violence occurs, protecting victims; and
d. providing emergency assistance.

Article 13
Letter a Sufficiently clear.
Letter b What is meant by "basic services" includes, among others: the right to education, health, and access to parents during the handling process.
Letter c What is meant by "equal protection" relates to status, citizenship, race, skin color, sex, language, belief, religion, politics, ethnicity or social life, property, disability, birth, or other status.
Letter d Sufficiently clear.
Letter e What is meant by "obtaining freedom" is being free to express his/her views on all matters, including those related to legal processes, care and temporary protection, as well as the identification and implementation of subsequent solutions.

Article 38
The duties and functions of FPKK as referred to in Article 37 paragraph (1) are:
a. coordinating and synchronizing prevention, services, and empowerment for victims of violence against women and children,
b. maintaining and developing FPKK in prevention, services, and empowerment of victims of violence through networking and a referral system,
c. conducting education on non-discrimination values toward women and children,
d. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence,
e. collecting, compiling, and presenting reports on data of victims of violence, and
f. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

Article 3
Victim Protection aims to:
a. prevent violence against women and children,
b. provide services to Victims, and
c. carry out empowerment of women victims of violence.

Article 13
Child victims of violence, in addition to receiving the rights as referred to in Article 12, also receive special rights, consisting of:
a. respect for survival, growth and development, basic services, equal protection, being free from various stigma, and/or obtaining liberty.

CHAPTER I

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Gorontalo Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Gorontalo.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
4. Regional Governance is the administration of government affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or ...
11. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Region to provide services in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
16. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and ... in the household.
19. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.

II. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and inherent disposition, without discrimination.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Gorontalo Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Gorontalo Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Gorontalo Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Gorontalo.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
4. Regional Governance is the administration of government affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or ...
11. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Region to provide services in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
16. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and ... in the household.
19. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.

9. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or ...
11. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Region to provide services in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
16. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and ... in the household.
19. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.

Article 21
(1) Efforts to prevent violence against women and children shall be carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government coordinated by the regional apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by:
a. establishing a working network in efforts to prevent violence,
b. the working network referred to in point 1 (one) is:
1) task force on acts of violence against women and children,
2) Bele lomongoditi moli,
3) Children's Forum,
4) Berlian (Bersama Lindungi Anak), and
5) Suami sayang istri,
c. establishing a violence prevention system:
d. conducting socialization regarding laws and regulations related to the protection of women and children victims of violence, and
e. providing critical education on the rights of women and children for the community.
(3) The establishment of Institutions and Procedures for implementing the tasks of the working network as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 39
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for Victims.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. establishing family partners at the kelurahan/village level by the community,
b. establishing women and children protection units within community organizations,
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights,
d. providing first aid to victims,
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

e. executive chairperson, and
f. executive vice chairperson.

Article 9
Neglect as referred to in Article 5 letter d is caused by:
a. acts that result in the failure to properly fulfill a child’s needs, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for the child’s care,
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for the child’s care,
c. acts of neglecting a person within the scope of their household, whereas under the law applicable to them or due to consent or an agreement they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person, and/or,
d. acts that result in economic dependency by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under that person’s control.

Article 12
Letter a What is meant by "to have their dignity respected as human beings" is upholding human rights.
Letter b Sufficiently clear.
Letter c Sufficiently clear.
Letter d What is meant by "obtaining information" is the right to obtain explanations, statements, ideas, and signs that contain value, meaning, and messages, whether data, facts or their explanations that can be seen, heard, and read that are presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology either electronically or non-electronically related to acts of violence.
Letter e Sufficiently clear.
Letter f What is meant by "compensation" includes: economic empowerment, repatriation costs, health coverage, and education or skills training.

Letter h What is meant by "complaint handling" is the availability of a special integrated service unit by officers.
Letter i Sufficiently clear.
Letter j What is meant by "assistance" includes among others: psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, clergy/religious leaders, advocates, and family members.

Article 11
Other violence as referred to in Article 5 letter f is committed due to:
a. threats of violence, which include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrain a person's fundamental freedom; and coercion, which includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something that is contrary to their own will.

Article 27
Accompaniment services as referred to in Article 25 letter b include:
a. accompanying victims during the examination and health recovery process,
b. accompanying victims during the medicolegal process,
c. accompanying victims during the examination process at the Police, Prosecutor's Office and court,
d. monitoring the interests and rights of victims in the examination process at the Police, Prosecutor's Office and Court,
e. maintaining the privacy and confidentiality of victims from all parties who have no interest, including coverage by mass media,
f. coordinating with other companions, and
g. providing continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage.

Letter a Sufficiently clear.

Article 10
Exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter e is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others, acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial, and/or all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecent acts.
